GEM can bind to the hydrophobic sites of BSA or HISA, and the binding is accompanied by conformational changes.
the GEM binds to BSA or BSA via a static quench process with a high binding constant, and this binding process is accompanied by conformational change.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GEM can bind to BSA and H SA, and the binding of G EM to BSA or HS A induces the conformational changes and fluorescence quenching of BSA or H SA.
the binding of BSA or HISA with GEM was mainly due to hydrophobic interactions.

the binding of BSA and/or HSA to GEM was mainly due to the electrostatic interaction between the negatively charged GEM and positively charged amino acid residues in BSA and/or positively charged HSA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GEM binds to BSA and H SA with different binding constants and different binding sites.
